key_insight: Co-PiLOT combines a generative latent space with physics-informed black-box optimization to make inverse design feasible for complex microstructure-driven mechanics problems.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce expensive simulation trials when tuning microstructures or other high-dimensional engineering designs toward a target property.
method: Train a ViT-based encoder and diffusion/transformer decoders on ~80k EBSD microstructure images to learn a compact latent representation.
Use the decoder as a learned validity prior and a self-segmenting orientation codec to map latent candidates back into solver-ready grids.
Optimize the latent space with MERIDIAN, which adds deep-kernel GP uncertainty, feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On the magnesium alloy inverse-design task, the ViT-FMDiT model achieved strong reconstructions (FID 27.86, MS-SSIM 0.178) and MERIDIAN reduced relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines within 160 simulations.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the learned decoder and latent manifold, so generalization and validity may weaken outside the training data distribution.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
